name: triauth-js
description: Official JavaScript client library for the triauth protocol. Password-less, decentralized single sign-on with keys published in DNS.

paragraphs: Sign in to websites with just your email address and no passwords.
Actually you don't even need an email address, just a domain will do.

triauth is a new decentralized protocol for password-less single sign-on where the user's web browser and domain vouches for them. Public keys are published as DNS TXT records under the user's own domain, and each login is signed by the web browser running on user's device and verified against those records.
features: This is the home of official triauth javascript client library.
Complete authentication flow is about 30 lines of code.
Add decentralized, password-less single sign-on to your website in an afternoon.

requirements.text: Sign in to websites with just your email address and no passwords.
Public keys are published as DNS TXT records under the user's own domain, and each login is signed by the web browser running on user's device and verified against those records.

If you require strict cryptographic integrity at the cost of losing compatibility with non-DNSSEC domains, set config.requireSecure = true (globally or as a per-call override) to have triauth-js enforce DNSSEC for you: any challenge-response result (and Triauth.check/Triauth.verify) that is not DNSSEC-secure is then rejected with error 404 instead of returning success.
